candidate.summary:
Confirmed the current stable SQLite version and recorded it, then verified the WAL documentation.

1. Current stable SQLite version = 3.53.4 (released 2026-07-24). Confirmed two independent ways on the official site:
   - Download page (https://sqlite.org/download.html): all current release artifacts are version 3.53.4 (e.g. "sqlite-amalgamation-3530400.zip", "SQLite version 3.53.4").
   - Release chronology (https://sqlite.org/chronology.html): newest entry is "2026-07-24  3.53.4".

2. Wrote just the version number into sqlite-version.txt (contents: "3.53.4\n", sha256 632cf989f3b8c2925dc35a67d06535db480cb97d53f78c14bb159f3de4e9bb04). Note: the write_file/read_file tools were not bound in this session ("tool ... is not bound to this member"), so the file was created and verified via the shell instead.

3. Fetched https://sqlite.org/wal.html and confirmed it is about WAL mode: page title "Write-Ahead Logging", with sections including "Activating And Configuring WAL Mode", "Persistence of WAL mode", "How WAL Works", "Checkpointing", and "Sometimes Queries Return SQLITE_BUSY In WAL Mode". It states WAL availability begins with version 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) and describes the WAL-reset bug fixed in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13).
evidence: web_fetch https://sqlite.org/download.html -> all artifacts labeled version 3.53.4 / filenames *-3530400.*
shell: printf '3.53.4\n' > sqlite-version.txt; cat/od/sha256sum -> contents '3.53.4\n', sha256 632cf989f3b8c2925dc35a67d06535db480cb97d53f78c14bb159f3de4e9bb04
web_fetch https://sqlite.org/wal.html -> title 'Write-Ahead Logging', includes 'Activating And Configuring WAL Mode' section
